## `garuda.excludes`

### `garuda.excludes.defaultpackages.exclude`

Remove individual entries from the "defaultpackages" list, matched by
their string representation. Everything else stays as shipped.

- **Type**: `list of anything`
- **Default**: `[ ]`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/programs.nix`

### `garuda.excludes.defaultpackages.excludeAll`

Drop every entry the Garuda modules would otherwise put into the
"defaultpackages" list (system packages, kernel parameters, nix-ld
libraries, home-manager modules, …). Useful for minimal installs.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/programs.nix`

### `garuda.excludes.home-manager-modules.exclude`

Remove individual entries from the "home-manager-modules" list, matched by
their string representation. Everything else stays as shipped.

- **Type**: `list of anything`
- **Default**: `[ ]`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/home-manager/home-manager.nix`

### `garuda.excludes.home-manager-modules.excludeAll`

Drop every entry the Garuda modules would otherwise put into the
"home-manager-modules" list (system packages, kernel parameters, nix-ld
libraries, home-manager modules, …). Useful for minimal installs.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/home-manager/home-manager.nix`

### `garuda.excludes.kernelparameters.exclude`

Remove individual entries from the "kernelparameters" list, matched by
their string representation. Everything else stays as shipped.

- **Type**: `list of anything`
- **Default**: `[ ]`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/boot.nix`

### `garuda.excludes.kernelparameters.excludeAll`

Drop every entry the Garuda modules would otherwise put into the
"kernelparameters" list (system packages, kernel parameters, nix-ld
libraries, home-manager modules, …). Useful for minimal installs.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/boot.nix`

### `garuda.excludes.nixldlibraries.exclude`

Remove individual entries from the "nixldlibraries" list, matched by
their string representation. Everything else stays as shipped.

- **Type**: `list of anything`
- **Default**: `[ ]`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/programs.nix`

### `garuda.excludes.nixldlibraries.excludeAll`

Drop every entry the Garuda modules would otherwise put into the
"nixldlibraries" list (system packages, kernel parameters, nix-ld
libraries, home-manager modules, …). Useful for minimal installs.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/programs.nix`

## `garuda.garuda-chroot`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.boot-uuid`

Provide the UUID of the Garuda boot partition

- **Type**: `string`
- **Default**: `null`
- **Example**: `"D9CB-2B11"`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.enable`

Enables mounting of the Garuda Linux root partition.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Example**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.nvidia`

Bind the NVIDIA device nodes into the container (host has an NVIDIA GPU).

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Example**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.pipewire`

Bind the host PipeWire socket into the container for native audio.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `true`
- **Example**: `false`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.root`

Specifies where the Garuda Linux root partition should be mounted

- **Type**: `string`
- **Default**: `"/var/lib/machines/garuda"`
- **Example**: `"/mnt/ssd/garuda"`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.root-uuid`

Provide the UUID of the Garuda root partition

- **Type**: `string`
- **Default**: `null`
- **Example**: `"f498b189-79c7-40e4-859e-fadc1496ee8e"`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.user`

The default user of the Garuda / NixOS subsystem

- **Type**: `string`
- **Default**: `null`
- **Example**: `"garuda"`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.wayland`

Bind the host Wayland socket into the container to allow running
GUI apps from within the Garuda installation on NixOS.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `true`
- **Example**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.garuda-chroot.waylandSocket`

Name of the host Wayland socket under /run/user/1000 to bind.

- **Type**: `string`
- **Default**: `"wayland-0"`
- **Example**: `"wayland-1"`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/mount-garuda.nix`

### `garuda.hardware.autoDriver.enable`

### `garuda.hardware.autoDriver.reportPath`

Path to the nixos-facter report (written by the installer).

Hardware baseline: CPU microcode updates, redistributable

### `garuda.hardware.laptop.enable`

Whether to enable laptop power/thermal tuning.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Example**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/hardware.nix`

### `garuda.hardware.nvidia.enable`

Whether to enable proprietary NVIDIA driver support with the latest drivers.

- **Default**: `false`
- **Example**: `true`

### `garuda.hardware.nvidia.nvidiaBusId`

PCI bus ID of the NVIDIA dGPU for PRIME offload

## `garuda.managed`

### `garuda.managed.config`

Path to garuda-managed.json, written by garuda-nix-manager.
It carries the managed settings — hostname, locale, timezone,
keymap, auto-detected virtualisation, and extra packages — merged
underneath your explicit configuration via gDefault, so anything
you set yourself always overrides the defaults.

- **Type**: `null or absolute path`
- **Default**: `null`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed`

## `garuda.mokka`

### `garuda.mokka.enable`

Mokka edition: calm dark Plasma 6 desktop in the Catppuccin
Mocha palette, with matching login theme, apps and defaults.
Mutually exclusive with garuda.dr460nized.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Example**: `true`

## `garuda.networking`

### `garuda.networking.enable`

NetworkManager (loopback, docker and libvirt interfaces unmanaged,
Wi-Fi powersaving off), legacy DHCP/wireless services disabled,
and the wireless regulatory database enabled.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Example**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/networking.nix`

### `garuda.networking.iwd`

Use iwd as the NetworkManager Wi-Fi backend.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Example**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/networking.nix`

### `garuda.networking.tweakKernel`

Lower-latency networking: TCP BBR congestion control with the
cake queueing discipline and a shorter TCP FIN timeout.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `true`
- **Example**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/networking.nix`

## `garuda.subsystem`

### `garuda.subsystem.enable`

Run this NixOS install as a subsystem inside Garuda Linux:
it derives certain settings from the Garuda installation,
imports the host's users, shares their home directories
and mounts the Garuda root filesystem for cross-system access.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed`

### `garuda.subsystem.import-networkmanager`

Bind-mount the Garuda host's NetworkManager system-connections
into this system, so Wi-Fi and VPN profiles are shared instead
of configured twice.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.enable`

Recreate the Garuda host users inside this system. Disable to
manage users purely via users.users instead.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.shared-home.enable`

Share the imported users' ~/.config, ~/.local and ~/.cache
between the Garuda host home and the NixOS home via bind
mounts, so app settings carry over to the subsystem.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.shared-home.uuid`

UUID of the Garuda BTRFS filesystem holding the @home
subvolume that the shared home directories are mounted from.
Set automatically from garuda-managed.json.

- **Type**: `string`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.users`

User accounts imported from the Garuda host (populated from
garuda-managed.json), keyed by username. Each entry recreates
the host user witht the same UID, home and admin rights inside NixOS.

- **Type**: `attribute set of (submodule)`
- **Default**: `{ }`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.users.<name>.home`

Home directory of the imported user, e.g. /home/garuda.

- **Type**: `string`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.users.<name>.passwordHash`

Hashed initial password, used as initialHashedPassword.

- **Type**: `string`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.users.<name>.uid`

Numeric UID, kept identical to the Garuda host user.

- **Type**: `signed integer`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.imported-users.users.<name>.wheel`

Whether the imported user gets wheel (sudo) membership.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed/subsystem/imported-users.nix`

### `garuda.subsystem.useGrub`

Install GRUB (device "nodev") so the Garuda host bootloader can
chainload this system. Disable when the host bootloader already
handles booting or another loader is used.

- **Type**: `boolean`
- **Default**: `true`
- **Declared in**: `internal/modules/base/managed`
